_note: Narration script for the Hypoglycaemia module (CPP-009-AO v4.1). Generated as one take; one paragraph per scene.

lines.head: Introduction
sentences: Hypoglycaemia.
What every Ambulance Officer needs to know.

lines.head: What it looks like
sentences: Hypoglycaemia can look like confusion, altered behaviour and sweating, and can progress to unconsciousness and seizure.
Measure the blood glucose level on every patient with an altered conscious state or altered cerebral function, including trauma and seizures, and especially children.

lines.head: The number
sentences: The normal range is usually above three point five millimoles per litre for adults and children, and above two point five for neonates.
This protocol applies when the B G L is below three point five.

lines.head: Least invasive
sentences: The aim is simple.
Use the least invasive treatment that raises the blood glucose.
Start with basic care and life support.

lines.head: Oral glucose
sentences: If the patient is two years or older, and has an adequate G C S to swallow the paste, a cough is a good indicator, give oral glucose, up to fifteen grams.
Request clinical support as appropriate.

lines.head: Glucagon
sentences: If oral glucose cannot be given, or does not work, consult the E O C Clinician.
They may advise intramuscular glucagon.
For patients six years or older, or twenty five kilograms or more, that is one milligram.
From two years up to six, or under twenty five kilograms, it is half a milligram.

lines.head: Under two years
sentences: For patients under two years, consult the E O C Clinician.
They may advise oral glucose gel, or intramuscular glucagon, half a milligram, and you should request clinical support.

lines.head: Giving it safely
sentences: Do the medication checks before you prepare a medication, before you give it, and again afterwards, with a second clinician whenever possible.
Check the medication, that it is in date, and the dose.
For an injection, the preferred site is the vastus lateralis, on the anterior lateral aspect of the mid thigh, not the side of the thigh.

lines.head: After treatment
sentences: If the patient recovers, consider offering complex carbohydrates to eat.
Provide transport, and notify the receiving facility.

lines.head: Wrap-up
sentences: So: measure the sugar, use the least invasive treatment first, and call the E O C Clinician if oral glucose fails.
Then try the treatment checker on this page.
